body.target_estimand: \(\Psi(\mathbb P)=\sum_{x=1}^dp_x\max_a\mu_{ax}\); when \(\mathbb P=\operatorname{Obs}(P)\) for a consistent, armwise-exchangeable causal completion, \(\Psi(\mathbb P)=V^\star(P)=E_P[\max_aE_P\{Y(a)\mid X\}]\).
body.estimand_functional: \(\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{JF}}=E[\Pi_{[0,1]}\{\sum_{x=1}^dT_x^{\mathrm{JF}}\}\mid O_1,\ldots,O_n]\), with \(\sup_{\mathbb P\in\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}}E_{\mathbb P}[(\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{JF}}-\Psi(\mathbb P))^2]\asymp_\epsilon\min\{1,d/[n\log(ed)]\}\); under the causal corollary, \(\Psi\{\operatorname{Obs}(P)\}=V^\star(P)\).

sampling_model.design: For each \(\mathbb P\in\mathcal D_{d,\epsilon}^{\mathrm{obs}}\), \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent observations with common law \(\mathbb P\).
sampling_model.units: The units are \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\), and the categorical cell masses \(p_x\) are unrestricted, including null cells.
sampling_model.treatment: Under \(\mathbb P\), \(A_i\in\{0,1\}\) has an unknown cell propensity \(\pi_x\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Auxiliary Poisson thinning creates independent pilot and evaluation counts. Pilot-local tensor Jackson approximation of the globally Lipschitz cell extension is lifted by centered factorial moments, clipped locally, projected globally, and Rao--Blackwellized conditional on all \(n\) observations.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The paper defines the unrestricted observed binary-outcome model by at most \(d\) categorical cells, cell propensities in \([\epsilon,1-\epsilon]\), and regressions in \([0,1]\), and proves estimation bounds for a signed linear treatment-effect functional rather than a cellwise maximum.
The paper constructs minimax-rate estimators for normalized two-distribution \(L_1\) distance by local polynomial approximation and proves the associated large-alphabet lower rate.
The paper pairs moment-matched priors with best approximation of absolute value and constructs asymptotically sharp estimators for a Gaussian nonsmooth functional.
The paper characterizes pathwise differentiability of the optimal value and gives online one-step inference at certain exceptional laws.
The paper obtains asymptotic inference for optimal policy values through softmax smoothing under controlled near-tie density and nuisance-rate conditions.
The paper constructs a local-moment estimator of a distribution up to permutation and proves plug-in universality for several symmetric discrete-distribution functionals.

The paper develops the generic large-alphabet architecture of polynomial approximation, sample splitting, and unbiased factorial-moment lifting for additive discrete-distribution functionals; it does not supply the coupled four-coordinate overlap-ratio maximum or the present all-regime frontier.

body.tldr: Relative to the archived downgraded predecessor \(\texttt{stat\_discrete\_optimal\_value\_minimax\_diagonal\_adaptive\_ratio}/\texttt{tv}\), this estimation upgrade replaces the certified \(d/n\) empirical-ratio upper bound by an explicit all-data Jackson--factorial estimator and proves the matched finite-sample risk \(\mathfrak R_{n,d,\epsilon}\asymp_\epsilon\min\{1,d/[n\log(ed)]\}\). A globally Lipschitz extension of the cell oracle permits one pilot-local tensor Jackson polynomial to handle null cells, off-cone pilots, unequal propensities, boundary means, and exact ties; centered factorial moments, local clipping, Poisson coupling, and Rao--Blackwellization yield the upper bound, while a dense moment-matching experiment, the exact normalized \(L_1\) slice, and padding yield the all-regime converse. The result settles uniform consistency exactly at \(d=o(n\log(en))\) and retains parametric mean-squared error exactly for bounded \(d\).

project_justification.gap: The closest accepted in-repository comparator, \(\texttt{stat\_discrete\_ate\_minimax\_loggap\_polynomial\_upper\_match}/\texttt{thm:sharp-minimax-fixed-interior}\), treats the signed aggregate \(\tau=\sum_xp_x(\mu_{1x}-\mu_{0x})\) on the same four-cell overlap cone and obtains mean-squared error \(n^{-1}+d^2/[n^2\log^2 n]\) for \(d\leq\rho_\epsilon n\log n\) using a heavy/light ratio-polynomial hybrid. It does not treat the cellwise maximum, whose decomposition contains an absolute tie contrast. The archived downgraded predecessor for the present target certifies only \(d/n\) achievability and therefore leaves a logarithmic gap and the region between \(d=o(n)\) and \(d=o(n\log n)\) unresolved.
project_justification.niche: The oracle maximum is a degree-one homogeneous functional of four observed cell masses. Its decomposition into a smooth average and a cellwise absolute treatment-effect contrast distinguishes it from the signed aggregate comparator. Its extension to the whole orthant is globally Lipschitz, so a positive tensor Jackson convolution can adapt pointwise at the cone vertex while retaining an exponential coefficient envelope in a centered local basis.
project_justification.fill: The explicit all-data Jackson--factorial estimator has uniform mean-squared error at most \(C_\epsilon\min\{1,d/[n\log(ed)]\}\), and the dense moment-matching, exact normalized \(L_1\), padding, and regular two-point constructions give the matching lower bound against every measurable estimator. Thus the note proves an all-regime optimal-value frontier rather than transferring the signed-aggregate rate. The archived downgraded predecessor is retained solely to document lineage on the identical assumptions and target.

body.related_work: The accepted in-repository result \(\texttt{stat\_discrete\_ate\_minimax\_loggap\_polynomial\_upper\_match}/\texttt{thm:sharp-minimax-fixed-interior}\) studies the same four-cell overlap cone but the signed aggregate \(\tau=\sum_xp_x(\mu_{1x}-\mu_{0x})\). It proves mean-squared error \(n^{-1}+d^2/[n^2\log^2 n]\) on \(d\leq\rho_\epsilon n\log n\) with a heavy/light ratio-polynomial hybrid. The present functional is \(\sum_xp_x\max_a\mu_{ax}=2^{-1}\sum_xp_x(\mu_{0x}+\mu_{1x})+2^{-1}\sum_xp_x\lvert\mu_{1x}-\mu_{0x}\rvert\), so its nonsmooth term is cellwise absolute rather than a signed aggregate; neither result subsumes the other and no rate is transferred between them. Zeng, Balakrishnan, Han, and Kennedy, \cite{ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024Discrete} [reused from the archived predecessor], Introduction, Theorems 1--2, and Discussion, formulate the same structure-free categorical adjustment problem and prove a logarithmically separated minimax analysis for linear treatment-specific means; their target has no maximum or tie surface. Jiao, Han, and Weissman, \cite{JiaoHanWeissman2018L1} [reused from the archived predecessor], Introduction, Theorem 3, Construction 2, Theorem 6, and Section VI, show that approximation must follow the equality diagonal for \(L_1\) distance and supply the normalized-distance lower theorem used on the exact equal-propensity slice; their unknown--unknown upper estimator does not apply to four observational masses with unknown arm denominators. Cai and Low, \cite{CaiLow2011L1} [reused from the archived predecessor], Lemma 1 and Sections 3.1--4, provide the approximation--moment dual for the absolute-value cusp and the fuzzy-hypothesis template adapted in the dense lower experiment. Luedtke and van der Laan, \cite{LuedtkeVanderLaan2016OptimalValue} [reused from the archived predecessor], Theorem 1 and Sections 4--7, characterize local nonregularity and online inference for the same scalar value, but do not analyze a growing unrestricted alphabet. Whitehouse, Chen, Austern, and Syrgkanis, \cite{WhitehouseChenAusternSyrgkanis2025} [reused from the archived predecessor], the static-treatment theorem and controlled-density lemma, regularize the maximum by softmax; their condition permits an atom at an exact tie but restricts near ties and nuisance rates, so it does not provide a uniform result for the present class. Han, Jiao, and Weissman, \cite{HanJiaoWeissman2018Local}, Introduction and Sections 2--3, establish cell localization and moment reconstruction for symmetric functionals, but their quotient forgets the four-coordinate grouping needed by causal ratios. Jiao, Venkat, Han, and Weissman, \cite{JiaoVenkatHanWeissman2015Functionals}, Sections III--IV, provide the generic large-alphabet architecture of polynomial approximation, sample splitting, and unbiased factorial-moment lifting for additive discrete-distribution functionals; they do not provide the coupled four-coordinate overlap-ratio maximum or the present all-regime frontier.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The estimator is explicit as a measurable Rao--Blackwellized finite-sample rule, but the conditional integration over auxiliary markings and the tensor coefficient calculation are not claimed to run in near-linear time or to be numerically stable at machine precision. The theorem gives constants depending only on fixed overlap, not a sharp leading minimax constant.
body.honest_scope: The formal target is the scalar value of the unrestricted oracle policy, not regret of a learned policy and not uniform confidence intervals. Fixed overlap is maintained; vanishing overlap, growing treatment count, and sharp leading constants remain outside the theorem. The accepted in-repository signed-aggregate theorem and the present cellwise-maximum theorem concern different functionals, so the comparison claims neither subsumption nor rate transfer. Proposition \(\mathrm{prop:equal\mbox{-}propensity\mbox{-}l1\mbox{-}reduction}\) is only a lower-bound sanity slice. Proposition \(\mathrm{prop:parent\mbox{-}reduction}\) records lineage to the archived downgraded predecessor: the model and estimand are identical, \(\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{JF}}=\widehat V_{n,d}^{\mathrm{ER}}\) only for \(2\leq d<D_0\), the matched rate implies the predecessor's bracket, and, along each fixed bounded alphabet sequence, minimax risk has two-sided \(n^{-1}\) bounds with constants allowed to depend on \(\epsilon\) and the finite bound \(D\). The exact constant is exposed separately in \(\mathrm{oeq:sharp\mbox{-}overlap\mbox{-}constant}\).
